title: A blast flattened a forest and left no crater

lines.text: In 1908, something exploded over Siberia and flattened a forest the size of a city. It left no crater.
It happened on the morning of June 30th, near the Tunguska River.
About 2,150 square kilometres of forest were knocked flat.
Estimates put the blast at several megatons, hundreds of times the Hiroshima bomb.
But when scientists finally reached the site, there was no impact crater at all.
The leading explanation: a space rock around 50 metres wide burst apart in the air, kilometres above the ground.
The shockwave did the damage, not an impact.
And if it had arrived a few hours later, it could have hit a populated city.

sources.claim: 30 June 1908 near the Podkamennaya Tunguska River; about 2,150 km² of forest flattened; no impact crater found
Energy estimates 3 to 50 megatons; leading explanation is an airburst of a 50 to 60 m stony asteroid 5 to 10 km up
